questions.question: If you ride on the right side of your lane while following a car, what happens?

options.text: You are in the best position to be seen.
The driver may not see you unless they check their side mirror.
The driver will know you are there.
You discourage other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may not see you unless they check their side mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane when following a car. This way, the driver will see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors much more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: What should you do for motorcycle safety?

options.text: Assume everything on your motorcycle works fine.
Check your motorcycle before every ride.
Check your motorcycle once a month.
Check your motorcycle twice a week.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your motorcycle before every ride.
questions.explanation: A small problem on a motorcycle is more serious than on a car. Always check your motorcycle thoroughly before you ride.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle, why should you ride in the left part of your lane?

options.text: It helps you see ahead better.
It makes it harder to see ahead.
It blocks your view of the other vehicle.
It encourages the other driver to speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you see ahead better.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane when preparing to pass. This helps you see ahead and makes other drivers more likely to see you.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel tired while riding?

options.text: Keep riding and hope you wake up.

questions.explanation: Do not ride if you are tired. On long trips, take a rest break at least every two hours to avoid getting too tired.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Protect you from wind blasts from other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Good lane position helps other drivers see you. It should protect you from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: How can you reduce your chances of having an accident?

options.text: Ride very close to the vehicle in front of you.
Only use your turn signal when you want to.
Stay alert and be ready to avoid a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay alert and be ready to avoid a crash.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, be visible to other drivers. Use your turn signals and brake light correctly. Keep space around your motorcycle. Always look ahead, behind, and to the sides of your motorcycle.

questions.question: For the best protection, jackets and pants should:

options.text: Cover your arms and legs completely.
Be loose and flap in the wind.
Only cover part of your arms and legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should cover your arms and legs completely. They should fit snugly but allow you to move freely. Leather or synthetic materials offer the best protection in a crash.

questions.question: Compared to a car, your motorcycle's brake light is:
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are not as noticeable as car brake lights. Flash your brake light before you slow down or stop to help other drivers notice you are braking.

questions.question: A rectangular sign can be a:
questions.explanation: Signs showing road rules, like speed limits, are usually rectangular with white background and black letters. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Can clothing help prevent injuries in a crash?

options.text: No, clothing does not protect you.
No, clothing is just a personal choice.
Yes, but only if it is very loose and flaps in the wind.
Yes, if a jacket and pants cover your arms and legs completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if a jacket and pants cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Proper clothing reduces injury in a crash. Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs, are made of sturdy material, and fit snugly without flapping in the wind.

questions.question: In a no passing zone, what can a motorcycle do?

options.text: A motorcycle may still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle may pass if it can finish before another vehicle approaches.
A motorcycle may pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: No passing zones prohibit all passing. You also cannot pass by riding off the main road.

questions.question: What is the main psychoactive substance in marijuana?
questions.explanation: THC (tetrahydrocannabinol) is the main psychoactive substance in marijuana.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. Inspect your motorcycle before every ride to avoid safety problems.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect you from?
questions.explanation: A face shield protects you from wind, dust, dirt, rain, insects, and pebbles. It also protects your face during a crash.

questions.question: Why should motorcycle riders turn their heads to look over their shoulders before changing lanes?

options.text: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles.
It catches the attention of other drivers.
To make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Always turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: When should a pre-ride inspection be done?
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride to prevent safety problems. Small technical issues are more dangerous on a motorcycle than on a car.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black lettering are warning signs. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When should a pre-ride inspection be done?
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. This only takes a few minutes and prevents dangerous problems before you enter traffic.

questions.question: What is an advantage of keeping a group of riders small?

options.text: A small group is less likely to be separated in traffic than a large group.
A small group can ignore traffic laws to stay together.
Riders will always be trying to catch up to the group.
It will be difficult to keep track of where everyone is.

questions.correctAnswerText: A small group is less likely to be separated in traffic than a large group.
questions.explanation: Small groups are better because other vehicles can pass them more safely. They are less likely to be separated by traffic or traffic lights. Riders don't have to speed to catch up.

questions.question: Before every ride, you should check all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check the rims and spokes for damage, the tire condition and tread, and all lights. You do not need to check the seat fabric.

questions.question: Why are signals important on a motorcycle?

options.text: They don't matter much because motorcycles are small.
They tell other drivers what you plan to do.
You only need to use them when other vehicles are nearby.
They are harder to use than signals on cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: As a motorcycle rider, you are at risk. Always use your turn signals when you change lanes or turn. Use them even if you think no one is nearby.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT required on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: In Nevada, motorcycles must have one or two headlights, a red taillight, a brake light, at least one rear reflector, front and rear brakes, turn signals (if made after 1973), mirrors on each handlebar, fenders on both wheels, footrests, a horn, and a muffler.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. How can you be more visible?
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen during the day. Always wear bright-colored clothing when riding, even during daylight hours.

questions.question: Which clothing item will NOT help reduce injuries in a crash?
questions.explanation: To reduce injuries, wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Choose clothing made of strong, durable materials for the best protection.

questions.question: What should you wear when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: You don't need a jacket if it's warm.
Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.
Wear shorts when it's hot out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket made of good material when riding, even in warm weather. Jackets help prevent dehydration. Also wear long pants and tuck in your shoelaces so they don't catch on the motorcycle.
